The Hollandse Kust (zuid) permit set the following rules to protect bats:

1. The cut-in wind speed of turbines will be 5.0 m/s at axis height during the period of 15 August to 30 September between 1 hour after sunset to 2 hours before sunrise (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description, p.33).
2. In case of a wind speed of less than 5.0 m/s at axis height, during the period referred to in part a, the permit holder will reduce the number of rotations per minute per wind turbine to less than 1 (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description, p.33).
3. Within two months after the end of the period referred to in part a, the permit holder will produce a report outlining how and in which way this regulation is implemented and submit it to the Minister of Economic Affairs (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description, p.33).

These rules were set under WFSD I and II Reg. 4.4 (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description, p.33).

The 50-year design wave height at the Hollandse Kust (zuid) site is 7.0 meters, and the 50-year design wind speed is 40.4 meters per second at 100 meters elevation relative to MSL (Hollandse Kust (zuid) Wind Farm Sites I and II - Project and Site Description, p.23).

Turbine HillOfTowie_18 is suspected of an anemometer calibration problem. The reason is that its peak Cp exceeds the Betz limit even after correcting for real air density, and the turbine's power curve is displaced +0.31 m/s from the farm-mean curve, consistent with a real nacelle anemometer bias.
